video_title: Long Gold And Short Semis Into Year-End? | Weekly Roundup
gist: Tony Greer joins the Forward Guidance hosts after the Democratic midterm sweep to argue the election was a known event that kicked off an AI/semis bubble unwind, with SMH having room to ~350. Their year-end playbook: long gold and miners, long bonds (October low is in), short semis, plus homebuilders and a tactical oil long, while December Fed hike odds look mispriced.

themes.theme: Post-midterm blue sweep and the 2018 analog

insights.claim: A co-host argues the Democratic midterm sweep was largely known in advance, so the election is not a clearing event but the start of new policy uncertainty (data centers in Texas under a Democratic governor, possible state-level AI/data-center moratoria, chip glut risk, government shutdown threats).
insights.speaker: co-host
insights.so_what: Post-election uncertainty for the AI/capex trade cannot be priced in a day; discount current conviction.
insights.quote: what the midterms represent are just the start of the uncertainty

insights.claim: The 2018 Trump midterm is cited as an analog: the S&P 500 sold off from the day after the midterms into late December 2018.
insights.speaker: co-host
insights.so_what: Suggests risk of a seasonal-defying selloff into year-end 2026.
insights.quote: the S&P puked from day after midterms all the way to late December

insights.claim: Inverted midterm-year seasonality charts fit 2026 price action: they peak in early October, fall, bounce, and fall again into year-end.
insights.speaker: co-host
insights.so_what: Implies weakness into December rather than the typical post-midterm rally.
insights.quote: If you flip those, they all peaked early October, down, bounced down again, and basically into year end.

insights.claim: The post-election rally (solar, crowded shorts squeezed, three-sigma sector moves) was mostly positioning and hedges rolling off, not a real signal, and it reversed the next day.
insights.speaker: co-host
insights.so_what: Do not read hedge roll-offs as directional conviction.
insights.quote: Don't Don't take hedges being rolled off as like real signal.

insights.claim: Tony Greer counted 14 S&P sectors with two-sigma-plus rallies and five with three-sigma rallies (retail, finance, consumer discretionary, airlines, home construction, broker dealers) the day after the election, all of which reversed the next day, signaling leverage blowups.
insights.speaker: Tony Greer
insights.so_what: Cross-sector extreme moves in both directions indicate forced deleveraging rather than fundamental repricing.
insights.quote: We had 14 sectors yesterday in the S&P with two sigma rallies or more and five sectors with three sigma rallies

insights.claim: Hosts argue the market forgot that, after losing the midterms, Trump and Bessent have no incentive to prop up markets because they can blame Democrats, having warned of a depression if Democrats won.
insights.speaker: co-host
insights.so_what: Removes the perceived 'Trump put' as a support for equities.
insights.quote: he has no incentive him and Bessant to prop this market he has the Democrats to point to

themes.theme: AI/semis bubble unwinding and IPO supply

insights.claim: Tony Greer is short semiconductors, arguing the AI bubble is bursting and that SMH, trading around 455 after coming off the 600s, has room down to about 350 before support.
insights.speaker: Tony Greer
insights.so_what: Concrete downside target for semis short into year-end.
insights.quote: There's room to 350 before there's support.

insights.claim: Semis rallied about 75% from April into the SpaceX IPO, which marked the top after roughly a year of consolidation; Greer views that IPO high as as significant a top as the October bond low is a bottom.
insights.speaker: Tony Greer
insights.so_what: IPO-at-the-top pattern signals distribution; treat rallies as shortable.
insights.quote: with the SpaceX IPO as the cherry on top at the dead ball high

insights.claim: The upcoming Anthropic IPO, a couple of weeks away, could be pushed into a Nasdaq 5-10% lower, and traders waiting to short on a mid-November sell-the-news event were pre-empted by the early November selloff.
insights.speaker: Tony Greer
insights.so_what: IPO supply is landing into a weakening tape; timing short entries around it is now harder.
insights.quote: they could be heaving this into a NASDAQ that's 5 10% lower from here

insights.claim: Hosts argue sell-side bullishness (Goldman initiating CoreWeave at buy as its credit came undone; JP Morgan's $500 SpaceX target with stock near 140) exists to sell AI capex financing and the Anthropic IPO to retail, while a roughly $500 million portfolio of data center loans was put up for sale in a rare auction days after the Democratic sweep.
insights.speaker: co-host
insights.so_what: Sell side says buy while holders liquidate data-center credit: a distribution tell.
insights.quote: a roughly $500 million portfolio of data center loans have been up for sale all at once in a rare auction

insights.claim: To get the SpaceX IPO done, access was opened down to roughly 25k accounts at Fidelity, which the hosts frame as retail being used as exit liquidity for AI-era IPOs.
insights.speaker: Tony Greer
insights.so_what: Broadening retail IPO access is a late-cycle sign.

insights.claim: Index concentration means a 10% one-day drop in Nvidia forces a big S&P decline; if Mag 7 falls another 10%, the S&P sits below its 200-day moving average and could incur real damage.
insights.speaker: Tony Greer
insights.so_what: Tech concentration makes the index hostage to the AI unwind.
insights.quote: if Nvidia is off 10% in a day, you know, the S&P is going to be down big

insights.claim: The selloff is an equity-only, long/short pod deleveraging (with a multi-strat returning capital) while bonds have barely moved since the election, which Greer reads as bond-market strength.
insights.speaker: co-host
insights.so_what: Watch for broadening beyond equities as the next leg risk; so far it is contained.
insights.quote: bond market hasn't moved since the election

insights.claim: Hosts note that shorting Elon Musk's companies and Trump-linked crypto coins (down about 30%) were the obvious missed trades after the Democratic sweep.
insights.speaker: co-host
insights.so_what: Politically-linked assets reprice quickly on power shifts.

themes.theme: Bond low is in; rate hikes mispriced

insights.claim: Tony Greer believes the long-bond low made in October is a durable bottom, citing max bearish sentiment, an Economist cover, and RSI around 8 in the long bond after a historically long selloff.
insights.speaker: Tony Greer
insights.so_what: Anchor for staying long duration and buying dips in bonds.
insights.quote: RSI at like eight in bonds

insights.claim: Greer argues oil would need a sustained rally above $110 for bonds to even approach their October low again.
insights.speaker: Tony Greer
insights.so_what: Sets the oil level that would invalidate the bond-bottom thesis.
insights.quote: we're going to need to see like a sustained rally above $110 for bonds to re to even approach that low

insights.claim: Markets still price roughly an 80% chance of a December Fed hike and the two-year yield remains above fed funds, which the hosts see as mispriced given a shift toward growth slowdown as AI capex and the wealth-effect-driven top of the K-shaped economy weaken.
insights.speaker: co-host
insights.so_what: Short-end rates are set up to rally if hike odds collapse.
insights.quote: there's still 80% chance of a hike in December

insights.claim: In 2018 the market bottomed when Fed hike expectations were removed; similarly, October 2026 hike odds fell from 72% to near zero after a flurry of Fed speakers before the midterms.
insights.speaker: co-host
insights.so_what: A repricing of December hike odds could mark the equity bottom.
insights.quote: October was at 72. It went down to zero basically

insights.claim: Greer contends the hikes are priced to fight energy inflation, yet gasoline is cheap on an inflation-adjusted basis and there is no major CPI inflation, so the inflation fear is a grocery-store 'mind virus' rather than a market reality; the latest hot PPI was ignored by bonds.
insights.speaker: Tony Greer
insights.so_what: Supports the view that December hike odds collapse if tech keeps falling.
insights.quote: gas is dirt cheap still. dirt cheap on an inflationadjusted basis

insights.claim: A co-host frames Q4 2018 as the analog: a new Fed chair struggling with press conferences, hiking on a false notion of strong growth, a roughly 20% Nasdaq drawdown, then the Powell pivot.
insights.speaker: co-host
insights.so_what: Expect a policy pivot after a sharp tech drawdown.

themes.theme: Long gold, real assets and commodities into year-end

insights.claim: Tony Greer's favored year-end trade is long gold (and gold miners), short semis, long bonds, with natural resources, E&Ps, industrials and basic materials expected to survive while tech reprices.
insights.speaker: Tony Greer
insights.so_what: Core pair trade: long gold / short semis.
insights.quote: I think in the end we're going to learn though that natural resources and commodities are going to live through this and tech is just going to have to repric

insights.claim: Gold's dip to roughly 3,800-3,950, below summer lows, followed by a quick recovery to 4,100 bid with no follow-through selling, is a look-below-and-reclaim pattern that often marks bottoms; a Democratic return to power revives the debasement trade.
insights.speaker: Tony Greer
insights.so_what: Failed breakdown is a buy signal for gold.
insights.quote: the kind of dip that bottoms are often made of

insights.claim: Gold miners filling all breakout gaps back down to 75 and holding is a precondition for Greer to get excited about miners, after a 150% year last year left them over-owned.
insights.speaker: Tony Greer
insights.so_what: Gives a level-based entry condition for miners.
insights.quote: 150% year in gold miners last year. Everybody piled in.

insights.claim: Greer argues gold is doing exactly what it should by holding above 4K and not falling while equities break down; the main risk is forced liquidation from the semi bubble popping.
insights.speaker: Tony Greer
insights.so_what: Gold as a store of value amid an equity unwind, subject to liquidity draws.
insights.quote: gold's doing exactly what the [ __ ] it's supposed to be doing

insights.claim: A co-host notes that DXY looks bullish yet USD/JPY is failing at a retest of its 200-day from below, consistent with safe-haven yen, bid bonds and a gold bottom, pointing toward safety assets in vogue rather than high-beta momentum.
insights.speaker: Felix
insights.so_what: Cross-asset tell favoring defensive positioning.

insights.claim: Greer keeps the dollar in a 98-102 range as his speedometer and won't act unless it breaks out.
insights.speaker: Tony Greer
insights.so_what: Range-break in the dollar is the trigger to reassess.

insights.claim: Greer still sees Bitcoin's blue-sky breakout intact and holds a small position despite a $6 billion hack denting crypto's credibility.
insights.speaker: Tony Greer
insights.so_what: Crypto holding up technically amid the equity selloff.
insights.quote: crypto looks fine to me

insights.claim: Greer would go home long a small crude oil position near its 200-day moving average, risking about $2, betting Trump's repeated Iran peace-talk headlines won't hold.
insights.speaker: Tony Greer
insights.so_what: Asymmetric long oil with tight stop against headline-driven dips.
insights.quote: just be long it and risk $2

insights.claim: A peace deal with Iran that drops oil $10-20 would be very bullish for markets, lifting industrials and miners, but Greer does not trust that the conflict is over despite pullbacks in diesel and crack spreads.
insights.speaker: Tony Greer
insights.so_what: Oil is the swing factor for both bonds and cyclicals.
insights.quote: I don't trust that we're making peace with Iran

insights.claim: Headline-driven oil moves, such as a Pete Hegseth removal headline that knocked oil down about 8%, keep traders from putting size on oil.
insights.speaker: co-host
insights.so_what: Position-size oil small given headline volatility.

insights.claim: Greer flags home construction (XHB, ITB) as a sneaky long: homebuilders are roughly unchanged on the year despite $7 diesel, ~7% mortgage rates and $110 oil, with a flat bottom that responds to the bond-market bottom.
insights.speaker: Tony Greer
insights.so_what: Relative strength under maximal headwinds plus a bond bottom favors upside.
insights.quote: they're unchanged on the year. Unched.

insights.claim: Greer's entry framework for a stock that has already popped: a resting bid below, a buy-stop above, and an egg timer forcing a 20% initial position by Friday's close if neither fills, then adding 25% pieces and adjusting daily.
insights.speaker: Tony Greer
insights.so_what: Practical method to gain exposure without chasing.
insights.quote: I have to put 20% of the position on by the bell on Friday

insights.claim: Greer distinguishes risky-price trades from non-risky ones, applying tighter, separate risk parameters to risky trades, and stresses managing positions aggressively in a tape of alternating three-sigma days.
insights.speaker: Tony Greer
insights.so_what: Separate risk regimes by trade type in volatile markets.
insights.quote: stick with the trades that are working and manage the living [ __ ] out of them
